source_notes.label: Mg feed controls hierarchical morphology
source_notes.summary: At fixed 20 mM CaCl2, the source reports regular rhombohedra without Mg, elongated rhombohedra at 10–20 mM Mg2+, dumbbells at 40 mM, and stacked spheres over 50–60 mM. The 60 mM images illustrate the latter range; no separately labelled 50 mM batch is invented. At 100 mM, the identified deposit is amorphous calcium carbonate with a smooth planar surface.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1, 3–4 and morphology discussion

source_notes.label: Three structural scales must remain distinct
source_notes.summary: Macroscopic architectures comprise triangular submicron units, described as several hundred nanometers wide, which contain nanocrystals. At 20 mM, SEM describes nanocrystals smaller than 50 nm and HRTEM resolves 5–20 nm mosaic domains. At 40/60 mM, surface crystallites are reported smaller than 20 nm; the 40 mM fractured radial interior separately contains 20–30 nm crystallites. These observations are not a single averaged particle size.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 4–6 and size descriptions

source_notes.label: Mg substitution and excess amorphous material
source_notes.summary: The (104) calcite peak shifts to higher angle and broadens with Mg feed. Substitution inferred from lattice contraction is lower than total Mg measured by ion chromatography, suggesting Mg outside the crystal lattice. The abstract states ca. 6% maximum substitution; exact per-feed values are only graphed and are not digitized here. The authors propose that excess Mg stabilizes ACC, suppressing regular growth and producing connected nanocrystals; this is a mechanistic interpretation, not a measured growth rate.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–4, Abstract, Figure 2 and mechanism

source_notes.label: Substrate selection is qualified
source_notes.summary: FTO deposits are predominantly calcite with (104) parallel to the substrate. Bare-glass deposits and solution precipitates instead contain calcite, vaterite and aragonite; their Mg feed and physical batch crosswalk are unspecified. SnO2 diffraction belongs to the substrate. Lattice matching is proposed, while the selective nucleation mechanism remains unclear.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, Crystal Structure comparison

source_notes.label: SI calibration versus product evidence
source_notes.summary: SI Figure S1 plots reference lattice spacings from database entries for calcite, high-Mg calcite, dolomite and magnesite; these are not new products or measured current unit cells. SI Figure S2 is the source FTIR series at 0, 10, 20, 40 and 100 mM Mg. Its band assignments support calcite versus ACC and water, without turning every listed band into a measured peak for every specimen.

source_notes.label: Reported setup and missing duration
source_notes.summary: Each vessel contains 50 cm3 precursor solution and FTO substrate under a polymer cover with several pinholes. Two vessels share a 750 cm3 desiccator and 4.0 g ammonium carbonate CO2 source at 25 °C. Deposition time, pH, post-treatment, substrate dimensions and pinhole geometry are unreported. The shared carbonate charge is not duplicated into per-vessel charges.

evidence_conflicts.summary: Figure 3b caption assigns 100 mM while its explanatory sentence and main p.3 also say above 100 mM. The measured 100 mM trace/image remains 100 mM; no extra >100 mM recipe is invented.

Main p.3 calls the Figure 6 20 mM specimen dumbbell calcite, whereas the Figure 3 discussion assigns elongated rhombohedra to 10–20 mM and dumbbells to 40 mM. Exact 20 mM figure linkage is retained without resolving the morphology wording.

Main p.2 reports <20 nm crystallites in dumbbells/spheres; p.3 Figure 5 fracture discussion gives 20–30 nm for the 40 mM radial interior. These are separate observations, not averaged or silently reconciled.
Figure 6b displays a 0.31 nm (104) lattice label and a bottom scale label printed as 4mm; the source crop is unchanged, and the anomalous scale label is not treated as a measured particle size.
